claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

claimant_dispute_unresolved.description: Whether two responsible claimants cannot agree who should claim Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child I'm asking about. His name is Alex and he's 18 years old. He lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 18, I need to understand his current situation to determine eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he in sixth form, college, or an approved training course?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's studying for his A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Since Alex is 18 and in approved education, he may still qualify.

**Are you currently living in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment.

**Does Alex live with you at home, or do you contribute financially to his upkeep?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually there's a bit of a situation there. His other parent and I are both responsible for him, and we can't really agree on who should claim the Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining that situation. This is actually addressed in the Child Benefit rules.

According to the rules, two people cannot get Child Benefit for the same child. If you and Alex's other parent are both responsible for him and cannot agree on who should claim, HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) will make the decision about who will receive it.

**Is anyone currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex at the moment, or has neither of you made a claim yet?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Neither of us has made a claim yet. We've been going back and forth about it, but no one has actually claimed it so far.

## Eligibility Assessment Result

Good news! **You are ELIGIBLE to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

### Here's why:

✓ **Alex is 18 and in approved education** - He's studying for his A-levels, which qualifies as approved education. Child Benefit can continue for children under 20 who stay in approved education or training.

✓ **You live in the UK** - You meet the residency requirement.

✓ **Alex lives with you** - This means you're responsible for him.

✓ **No one is currently claiming** - Since neither you nor Alex's other parent has made a claim yet, you're free to apply.

### Important points to note:

- **Only one person can claim** - You and Alex's other parent should try to agree on who will claim. If you both submit claims and can't agree, HMRC will decide who receives the benefit.

- **High Income Child Benefit tax charge** - Be aware that if you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay a tax charge on the Child Benefit received.

You can proceed with making a claim for Child Benefit for Alex. If you'd like, I can advise you that you should ideally reach an agreement with Alex's other parent first to avoid any complications.
